title: Prayer at Harmandir Sahib and the March to Battle

blocks.text: The ceremonial movement now becomes a public procession. Carrying the Khalsa standard a Singh moved in front, the war drums sounded, and gifts were distributed like alms from a wedding household as the jatha advanced through the sacred precincts.

The heart of the page is the prayer. Standing before the Guru in Harmandir Sahib, Gurbakhsh Singh bows, circles the shrine, and asks that his faith in Guru's ideology be vindicated so that his death may truly serve the Panth rather than merely display personal bravery.

At the same time the enemy prepares in its own way. Gilja Pathans had covered themselves with steel helmets and armours, yet among the Singhs each one promised to sacrifice ahead of the other, turning the contrast between heavily protected soldiers and lightly equipped martyrs into a test of conviction.
